A logger reading stands only where a plain run of the same unit agrees with it. A unit whose arms background a function gets the plain pair or a by-text citation, never the logger alone.

An instrument that shadows a command name changes what `command -v` answers, so a fixture that captures its real tool that way runs a different program. That caused this batch's 1,724-process burst and the hang. And a logger keyed on `git init` and `cp -R` cannot see a world built with `mkdir` and `printf`, so its "0 repeats" is a floor, not a count.

Deviations from a pure move, each named:
- `self-update-gate.sh` ports `SELF_SRC` to `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`, and its `gate_load_preclassify` rewrites the `"$0"` inside the eval'd `machinery_paths()` to the loaded preclassify path (`GATE_PRE_SRC`), so an in-process gate resolves the manifest beside that file.
- `preclassify.sh` ports its `_pc_d0` case to `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` and `setup_sited_paths()` to `${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}` (both preclassify fixtures call it in process; apply.sh evals its text from the preclassify.sh beside it, so the eval'd copy resolves the same directory). `machinery_paths()` and the `SETUP_SITED_PATHS=` line keep `$0` and are byte-identical to the base: self-update-gate.sh, unregistered-drift.sh and three fixtures eval `machinery_paths()`'s text, reconcile-blocking-list runs it under `bash -c`, where `BASH_SOURCE[0]` is empty, and apply-restamp-theirs pairs this preclassify.sh with a pre-R1 apply.sh that extracts the `SETUP_SITED_PATHS=` line under `bash -c`. Left open: an in-process preclassify run whose `skill_commit` differs from BASE resolves `machinery_paths()`'s manifest beside the caller, not beside preclassify.sh.
- `render-agent-definitions.sh` ports its two `$0` reads (the root walk's start and its refusal text) to `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`; `retired-tokens.sh` ports its `SELF` case and `self-update-fixtures.sh` its `SELF=` line the same way.
- preclassify-rename-row: preclassify refuses a git failure by `kill -USR1 "$PC_TOP"` under `trap 'exit 2' USR1`, which in process would signal the fixture. Each in-process call runs in a background subshell that learns its own pid over a fifo and shadows `kill` to signal that subshell (`mkfifo` is added to tools.decl). Cell mE gives the call an explicit fresh memo directory where the base unset `AI_DLC_RECONCILE_MEMO` for a separate program. preclassify-mode-bucket forces no git failure and ignores USR1.
- askuserquestion-citation's P6 runs a relocated copy of the subject as a program, an untagged start by design (the walk from the script's own location is the property).
- suite-content-key drops a failure-only diagnostic and drives the hook spans through a `bash()` shim: no `command -v`, `type` or `which` sits in the FIXTURE_POOL, SUITE_STEP or SUITE_BANNER spans, the pool's bash calls pass through, and the step's calls of the key script are answered in process.

Deviations the hands reported:
- **Not using `lib/inproc.sh`.** P2 reads `. "$1"` as an unrouted drive or as an unpaired source wherever a fixture declares an unguarded bash subject. So these fixtures source the subject in a stripped subshell paired with `fx_inproc`. Superseded since 0.1165.0 (BL-1164): P2 exempts `lib/inproc.sh`'s own source lines at the library (the INPX block of `scripts/validate-fixture-invocations.sh`) and judges each `inproc_load`/`inproc_run` call instead; the remaining cause is a call operand no literal path resolves in such a fixture (`:1013`, unpaired by `:1026`), which a literal-tail operand (`"${1%/*}/<subject>"`) removes. The measured cause was the call operand: `inproc_run "$_f"`, `"$1"` or `"$HOOK"` resolves to no literal path, and in a fixture declaring an unguarded subject `scripts/validate-fixture-invocations.sh:1013` reads that as a drive and `:1026` leaves it unpaired. C3b moved all three onto `inproc_load`/`inproc_run` with literal-tail operands (BL-1164, LANDED).
- **Not using `lib/inproc.sh` for another reason.** fixture-git-env-seam's `vf_ip` (unit g) uses a subshell source because, at 747f89054, declaring the library let the inner setup-config-drift run past its own source and failed J7.

  - `FAIL  R fixture-git-env-seam: core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/unregistered-drift.sh declares 4 start(s) against 0 cell(s); core/scripts/validate-audit-anchors.sh declares 4 start(s) against 0 cell(s)`

  R counts only the seam's own `cells.decl`, not the inner fixtures' cells that the dynamic judge credits. With the row restored and the two lines kept, the push's dynamic judge fails the other way: pregate read `FAIL (C stale): fixture-git-env-seam is a row of scripts/fixture-inprocess-allowlist.txt but now passes C1-C5 (10 subject start(s), 10 tagged, 0 covered by a nested row)`. So this release does not ship the two `cells.decl` lines. Without them the inner tags are uncredited, the row is genuinely needed, and the seam's counted run reads C EXEMPT. `--derive` rewrites the row's reason to name both subjects. Owed, in order:

## BL-974 — a record-format error in a shard or repair part is found by the lead's join, so one malformed line costs a resume round trip

**DEFECT (efficiency).** An adversary or remediator seals its part, the lead runs the merge or join, the join refuses the part on one line (an `artifact_sha:` stem in the provenance block, an `edit:` line that does not resolve, a coverage gap in the part record), and the lead resumes the finished agent to correct that line. Population for every figure: graph's Claude Code transcripts, 151 lead and 6,018 subagent, read only, window end 2026-11-11T10:30:00Z, extracted by `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/scripts/extract.py` with the s321/s322 edge at 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z; s322 is partial (planning complete, 3 of 8 stories done). In-session time only; handoff gaps are excluded by ruling. Resume messages to finished subagents, classified by their text: s321 13 join or merge refusals with 4.5 agent-hours of idle before the resume (21 minutes each); s322 16 with 11.2 agent-hours (42 minutes each). Each loop is also a lead turn to diagnose, a message, and a second join. Dollars: about $30 across the 29 loops, estimated at about $1 a resume; not measured per loop. The idle is agent idle, an upper bound on wall clock, because other agents may run meanwhile. Instances: s322 `requirements-p2/6.md` (`artifact_sha:` stem), s322 `requirements-repair-p1/1.md` (`edit:` line of F-1), s321 `stories-party-repair-p1/15.md` (coverage gap at line 112).

Fix direction, not built: the writer runs the join's own per-part check before it seals, so the refusal reaches the agent while it still holds the context. `--check-part` exists and the s322 agents ran it clean before the join refused them, so the gap is the difference between what `--check-part` checks and what the join and merge refuse. Close that difference in the per-part check; do not add a second checker. False-positive set and consumer cost unmeasured.

Step: requirements
Expected movement: join and merge refusals that end in a resume of the writing agent fall from 13 (s321) and 16 (s322 partial) a sprint to 2 or fewer, and no part that passed its own per-part check is refused by the join for a format reason.

## BL-975 — a subagent killed by an API connection error is noticed about an hour later

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Nothing reports a subagent whose run has ended on an API error. Population for every figure: graph's Claude Code transcripts, 151 lead and 6,018 subagent, read only, window end 2026-11-11T10:30:00Z, extracted by `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/scripts/extract.py` with the s321/s322 edge at 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z; s322 is partial (planning complete, 3 of 8 stories done). In-session time only; handoff gaps are excluded by ruling. On 2026-11-09 nine requirements remediators were dispatched together at 17:54Z (parts 1 to 9); four of them (parts 5 to 8) died within four minutes, and the lead later resumed five ("Repair part 1, 3, 4, 8, 9 brief"), four of them agents that had already delivered (see the premise-corrected paragraph below), between 19:00Z and 19:08Z with "Your run terminated on an API connection error (the cause is now resolved)". An earlier reading counted four resume messages, with 62 to 72 minutes of idle before each (4.2 agent-hours); the premise-corrected paragraph below supersedes it (five resumes, and each of the four dead seats ended in an unanswered `api-request`). s321 has none. Wall clock: 1.2 h for the event, on the critical path, since the round could not join without dead parts 5 to 8. Dollars: $0. Frequency: one event in the two sprints read. Judged on consequence: every occurrence stalls a whole round until the lead happens to look.

Fix direction, not built: the wait the lead is already armed on reports an agent that has exited without sealing its deliverable, or whose transcript has had no record for longer than a bound while a request is open, as FAILED with the agent named, instead of continuing to wait. `wait-for-deliverable.sh` already has FAILED and MISSING states; the question is what signal sets them for a dead agent. No timer-based retry is asked for.

Baseline: s322
Step: requirements
Expected movement: a beat names a dispatched agent whose last record is an unanswered api-request within `AI_DLC_OPEN_REQUEST_SECS` (1200 s) plus one 60 s check of that request, and an agent with a harness failed notice at its next check, while the lead can take a turn. Deviation, stated plainly: the reachable bound for the open-request arm is about 21 minutes after the last send (1200 s plus one 60 s check), and that does NOT meet the entry's original "under 10 minutes" wording. The harness-failed-notice arm still fires at its next check.

Decision rule: the step-value ruling, "A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`). Related: BL-538 (wake beats), BL-576.

Receipt: `verify: manual`; the mechanism's test is the behavioural fixture `core/fixtures/wait-beat-liveness`, which drives the wait over agents that died without their deliverable; the entry closes only on the `Outcome measured:` line its PARTIAL paragraph names. ## BL-972 — a pending AskUserQuestion holds the lead, so a lane that finishes during the question waits for the answer

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Population for every figure: graph's Claude Code lead transcripts and their subagent transcripts, read only, to 2026-11-11T10:30:00Z: 247 asks over s317–s322, with sprints from the `EDGES` in `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/scripts/extract.py`. s322 is partial. In-session time only; handoff gaps are excluded by ruling. Measured by `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322/scripts/ask_split.py` (output `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322/out/ask_split.txt`). Its per-sprint call counts and hours equal `operator_asks.py`'s for s317–s321. A wait is FINISHED-INSIDE when a subagent of the same lead session, started before the ask, wrote its last record during it. FINISHED-INSIDE minutes of all answer-wait minutes: s317 197 of 398, s318 271 of 811, s319 164 of 1113, s320 791 of 3052 (26%), s321 164 of 1576 (10%), s322 20 of 537. Those lanes are not joined or followed while the question is open. 290 task notifications were enqueued inside 77 of the 247 asks: 133 from agents, the rest from background Bash and Monitor. Every FINISHED-INSIDE ask has at least one agent notification. Yet no notification-carrying attachment or user record, and no lead assistant record, falls between any question and its answer (`DLV-INSIDE` 0, `ACT-INSIDE` 0). The script's self-probe proves both counters fire on a seeded inside record and stay at 0 on a same-message near-miss. 67 queue `remove` records do fall inside, and no record shows the lead's model receiving those before the answer. Control, asserted in the script: BL-841's 10-27 06:57Z ask scores FINISHED-INSIDE (95 min; two subagents finished inside it). Dollars: $0, a wait bills nothing.

The ceiling, stated so the entry is not read as owning the whole 26.3 h. The figure that names this defect is FINISHED-INSIDE. Most of s321's largest bucket, NONE-RUNNING, 1086 of 1576 minutes (69%), is deploy-validate asks with nothing running: 940 minutes, including the 645-minute "Router PUT" and the 264-minute "Merge #1305". These are operator actions on the serial deploy path, and no lead-side mechanism shortens an operator's answer. FINISHED-INSIDE also UNDERCOUNTS, in two ways. An agent that finished inside a wait and was resumed later has its last record after the ask: 3 asks outside FINISHED-INSIDE (397 min, all sprints) carry an enqueued agent `finished` notification. And background Bash and Monitor completions held by an ask are not bucketed at all. A lead that keeps working while a question is open could also dispatch ready lanes inside a wait of any bucket, and no transcript says where those were.

**Correction (2026-11-11, b255 F4b).** `ask_split.py` now deduplicates asks by `tool_use` id, so one s321 ask (23.9 min) that sits in two lead files is counted once. Under the deduplicated script the population above reads 246 asks, and s321 reads 1552 min with NONE-RUNNING 1063 and deploy-validate 916, against 247, 1576, 1086 and 940. FINISHED-INSIDE 164 is unchanged in minutes, and its share reads 164 of 1552 (11%) where the s321 figure above says 164 of 1576 (10%); NONE-RUNNING reads 1063 of 1552 (68%) where the ceiling paragraph says 1086 of 1576 (69%); any reading of s321's FINISHED-INSIDE minutes is therefore against 164 of 1552. The receipt's s321 ask-count baseline is `ask_split.py`'s deduplicated 56, not `operator_asks.py`'s 57. The two tools differ by that one duplicated row, so a closer must compare the ask count only within `ask_split.py`'s output, never across the two tools, and a count of 56 against 57 is not a fall in asks.

Fix direction, built at batch 256 (the Progress paragraph below). The contact shape is ruled. Immediately before the question, the lead joins every finished lane and dispatches every lane the question does not hold. The question itself goes out at once, in `AskUserQuestion`, unchanged. Asking in prose instead of the tool is NOT this fix: Rule 11(a) requires `AskUserQuestion` for an ambiguity question, and `core/hooks/ai-dlc-continue.sh:1637` records the measured failure of the prose form (the operator: "you haven't asked any question ... buried in the transcript"). No variant may suppress, batch away, defer or hold back a question. Immediately before each `AskUserQuestion`, the lead joins every finished lane and dispatches every lane the question does not hold, then asks at once in `AskUserQuestion`, unchanged. Option 2 (a non-blocking ask) and option 3 (accept the hold) were not chosen; option 2's harness question is filed as BL-994. ACT-INSIDE is dropped as the close key. It counts lead records positioned while the ask's tool_result is pending (`ask_split.py`'s ACT counter), so under a blocking ask a compliant lead reads 0 by construction, and DLV-INSIDE is 0 on every baseline ask. The literal first-draft HELD and DISPATCHED definitions failed too. Known limits of the pin: inside its subsection the `exact` row does not catch a drain instruction written as a `#####` sub-heading, because headings are skipped; one inside a fenced block; or one inside an HTML comment, because fences and comments are invisible to every test. The lead model reads raw markdown, so these are real survivors; closing them changes the fixture's grammar for every pin, which is a separate change.

Corrected HELD-AT-ASK is a regression guard, and it must read 0 on the closing sprint itself; s321 reads 0 asks above 0. Two older sprints carry a non-zero reading, each of 1, in the same file: s319 2026-10-23T00:20:46Z, which is api-request anchored, and s318 2026-10-12T03:13:16Z, which is fallback-anchored. Fallback-anchored means the ask has no `api-request` record, as in s317/s318-era transcripts, so the visibility boundary falls back to the last `user` record before the ask's message. That anchor agrees with the api anchor on all 207 api-anchored asks (FB-DISAGREE 0, with 39 asks on the fallback). The ask count is no longer a close condition: a fall is not credited to dispatch-then-ask, and none is required (batch 259 operator choice: design choices decided on the lead's recommendation are expected to lower it). Instead each Tier 2 `DECIDED_AUTONOMOUSLY` entry whose `**Decision/Question:**` line opens `source: recommendation`, in the closing sprint's `docs/escalations/pending.md` and `docs/escalations/pending-archive.md` (overridden entries are archived at retro close), is read by hand against Rule 11(a)'s reserved list, Rule 12 Tier 1 and the sort's Outside list; one reserved decision found decided instead of asked blocks the close. DISPATCHED-AT-ASK (s321 16 of 56, 28.6%, same file) is reported beside the close and is not a close condition. What else would satisfy a weaker receipt: a lead that holds a question back until its lanes drain. That turns every FINISHED-INSIDE wait into NONE-RUNNING and moves the minutes to 0 with the ask count intact. It is the deferral this entry forbids. The pure deferral dispatches nothing adjacent to the ask and reads ADJ 0, which is why the close is keyed on ADJ-DISPATCH and not on minutes. ADJ-DISPATCH alone cannot tell a lead that drains its lanes and then dispatches (it reads ADJ 1, HELD 0) from a compliant one (lead ruling, batch 256; `ask_split.py` probe (q) records it as the KNOWN LIMIT `defer_plus_bg`). DRAINED-AT-ASK is the column a reader checks for that shape. It is reported, never a close guard. DRAINED-AT-ASK, from the same file: s317 2 of 13, s318 2 of 26, s319 4 of 71, s320 4 of 63, s321 4 of 56 and s322 0 of 17. ADJ-DISPATCH and DRAINED-AT-ASK together: 1 of 56 in s321 (2026-11-08T16:24:12Z, the drain-then-dispatch shape in real data) and 0 in every other sprint, s320 included. ACT-INSIDE is no longer the key, because a compliant lead reads 0 on it by construction under a blocking ask. Fewer or faster-answered questions shrink every bucket without the mechanism, which is why no minutes figure and no ask count is credited to it. What this does not establish: whether every ready action was dispatched cannot be measured from a transcript, because no record names the actions that were ready. ADJ-DISPATCH shows a background dispatch next to the ask, not that it was the whole ready set. Subagents dispatched from another lead session are not joined, and asks issued from a subagent are not counted. Every column here is positional against a blocking ask. If the harness's ask mechanism changes (BL-994), check what these columns record under it before reading them. The step token is `extract.py`'s step for the asks carrying the most s321 FINISHED-INSIDE minutes (87 of 164).

## BL-1030 — gate 1 has no zero-seat GATE1-SKIP answer after a gate-3 rework, so a records-only rework that gate 3 did not ask to re-review would still dispatch a gate-1 seat

**NOTE (efficiency).** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-13. The second subject of BL-844's title, "a gate-3 rework re-runs gates 1 and 2", split out when BL-844 closed on its gate-2 subject. A gate-1 pass M >= 2 does ask about its delta: `core/scripts/gate-transition.sh` runs `partition-review-diff.sh --route` (`:317`, a one-seat record-only route) and `--narrow` (`:326`). What gate 1 lacks is a zero-seat answer. The `--gate1-rerun` question that records GATE1-SKIP and dispatches no gate-1 seat is asked only in the Rule A block (`:393`-`:397`), when a gate-2 pass M >= 2 opens, so a gate-1 plan opened after a gate-3 rework always dispatches at least one seat.

First reading (batch 257), by `docs/analysis/bl844-gate2-route-seats/derive-g3.sh` (output `out-g3.txt` beside it) at graph `main` c8ab65397, identical at 1449b5c72 apart from the ref line. Population, derived from the `-g3-p<M>.plan` listings: every story with a gate-3 plan at pass >= 2, s321 1-4 and 2-4 and s322 1, 3, 4, 6 and 8, so 9 gate-3 reworks (s320 has no gate plans). Each gate-1 and gate-2 plan is joined to its review file by `reviewed-sha:`.

Classification of each seat, from its review file, first rule that holds: (c) a gate-3 remedy, when the review's text before its `## Verdict` heading names gate 3 and a `Check <n>` (for example "It exists because gate-3 Check 19 FAILed pass 1"); (b) a same-gate re-review, when the same gate's previous pass reads NEEDS_REWORK; (a) a re-run, otherwise. Class (a) is this entry's subject.

Order and the tie convention: by the committer time t of the commit each plan's `sha:` names (plan and review files were committed in one batch per sprint, so their own commit times order nothing). Rework M owns a class (a) or (b) plan with t(g3 p<M-1>) < t <= t(g3 p<M>), and a class (c) plan with t(g3 p<M-1>) <= t < t(g3 p<M>). A remedy runs at the very sha the failed gate-3 pass judged, with no new commit, so the tie is broken by the remedy citation, never by time. The first version of this reading used the time window alone; it dropped s322 1 g1 p2 and mis-assigned s322 3 g1 p4, and its "6 of the 9 reworks re-ran neither gate" and "12 seats" are withdrawn.

Controls in the same run: s322 1 g1 p2 (a remedy at gate-3 p1's own sha) classifies (c), and s322 3 g1 p2 (the partitioned gate-1 pass after gate-3 p1) classifies (a); a seeded remedy line reads 1 before the verdict heading and 0 after it; the impossible story `ZZNOPE-8f3a1q` joins 0 plans; `GATE1-RERUN` appears in 0 graph plans and `GATE1-SKIP` in 18 (s321 12, s322 6), and the matcher reads a seeded `gate: rerun` / `route: rerun GATE1-RERUN:` plan, the form `core/fixtures/gate-transition/run.sh` asserts.

| s322 1 p2 | g1 p2 record-only (c, 0) | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| s322 1 p3 | g1 p3 serial, 0 reviewable files (c, 0) | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| s322 3 p2 | g1 p2 partitioned, 5 seats (a, 105); g1 p3 serial (b, 1); g2 p2 serial, records GATE1-SKIP (a, 1) | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| s322 3 p3 | g1 p4 serial (c, 0) | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| s322 4 p2 | g1 p2 serial (c, 1); g1 p3 serial (b, 3); g2 p3 serial (a, 4); g2 p4 record-only (b, 0) | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| s322 8 p2 | g1 p4 serial (c, 1) | 0 | 0 | 1 |

Totals: 15 seats after the 9 reworks, (a) 7, (b) 3, (c) 5; 3 reworks re-ran neither gate. Every class (a) seat reviewed a delta carrying code or test paths since the same gate's previous pass: s322 3 g1 p2 105 paths, s322 4 g2 p3 4 (`meta-gate.sh`, its test `test-s239-2-check26-discrimination.sh`, and two extension docs, `gate-validation-domain.md` and `deploy-validate-domain.md`), and s322 3 g2 p2 1 path, `server/test_live_smoke.py`, whose diff (`git diff c6ebe5c96d 9c572624c0`) changes executable test lines (`wait_until` and a `wait_for` call), not only docstrings. **PARTIAL (v0.1137.0) — the gate-1 mechanism shipped; the gate-2 record-only route after a gate-3 rework, the step prose and the Outcome measured: line are OPEN.** `core/scripts/gate-transition.sh` gate 1, pass M >= 2, now runs `g1_after_g3` before `--route`: when the story's newest `<idx>-g3-p<K>.plan` names a sha the pass M-1 reviewed-sha is an ancestor of or equal to, and the frozen sha is not that g3 sha (class (c), the remedy gate 3 asked for, always runs), and the pass M-1 review reads APPROVED through `merge-review-shards.sh --read-verdict` (class (b) always runs), it asks `partition-review-diff.sh --gate1-rerun` from that reviewed-sha. `GATE1-SKIP` writes a `gate: skip` plan, `manifest: none`, `route: skip GATE1-SKIP: ...`, no shard line, a `rule-a-base: gate1` line and a `next:` gate-2 command; the dispatch guard's ROLE TO GATE default arm already denies every seat on a `skip` plan. Remainder: (1) gate 2 after a gate-3 rework still reads `--route` from the QA pass M-1 file, whose findings are QA's, not gate 3's, so a records-only gate-3 rework still dispatches a full QA fan-out; keying the record-only route on gate 3's open findings needs a class field the adjudicator verdict does not carry. (2) `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/implementation.md` names no `gate: skip` plan; filed as BL-1131, its owner. (3) The Outcome measured: line this entry's Receipt names.

**Progress (batch 257, W12-13; the entry stays PARTIAL, `verify: manual` unchanged, no LANDED line).** Remainder (1), gate 2's record-only route keyed on gate 3's open findings, is not built in this release, and it stays OPEN as a DEFECT: the full QA fan-out it removes is reachable by mechanism and unobserved on record. ## BL-1124 — the push suite is throughput-bound, not pole-bound, and nothing that reads the push says so

**DEFECT.** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-15. Owner: `.githooks/pre-push` and `core/git-hooks/pre-push` (`pole_info_step`, `.githooks/pre-push:4514`; the `POLE-BOUND` throughput line at `:4537` and the dispatch-order header at `:4050`), `CLAUDE.md` (the "POLE-BOUND" sentence in the fixture-suite section), and `fixture_suite_step`'s work outside the pool.

B9 took 1084 s and B10's first push 1159 s, against a 15-minute target. Both pushes ran `── fixture suite (6-way)`, so the hook's default of 12 was not in force. The fixture step took 960 s and 1073 s, and the pole was 145 s and 147 s. These figures come from the gate logs and from a copy of `.git/ai-dlc-fixture-durations` taken at 08:59:23, after B10's re-push. B9 was green, so its units hold clean rows. Four of those rows are B10's re-push timings rather than B9's, and they total 32 s. B10 was red, so its units hold `@red` rows.

| push | units (dist + `@consumer`) | summed loaded cost | sum / 6 | fixture step | residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B9 | 124 (68 + 56) | 5289 s | 882 s | 960 s | 78 s |
| B10 | 166 (103 + 63) | 5992 s | 999 s | 1073 s | 74 s |

1. **The pool makespan is sum ÷ width.** B10's dispatch order is in its retained failure log, `ai-dlc-fixture-failures.20261115T134342Z.5180`. Simulating a 6-worker list schedule in that order over the recorded costs gives 999 s. A longest-first schedule on the actual costs also gives 999 s, so no dispatch order recovers anything. `.dur` is the worker shell's `$SECONDS` (`:3430`), which covers the whole unit. The pole is 15% of the makespan. `CLAUDE.md`'s "The suite is POLE-BOUND" and the hook headers at `:3184` and `:4050` are false for selections of this size, at width 12 as well (5992 ÷ 12 ≈ 500 s against 147 s). `pole_info_step` prints only the pole, so a reader of the push sees the wrong bound.
2. **About 75 s of each fixture step lies outside the pool, and that cost is fixed.** B9 had 78 s at 124 units and B10 had 74 s at 166, so the residual does not grow with unit count. `$SECONDS` reads whole seconds, so each unit's figure is off by less than 1 s in either direction, and that error cannot add up to a fixed residual. The rest is the work before and after the pool (the consumer-layout `install.sh` build, the read-set key selection, the trace report and the record merges), which no record times.
3. **Composition of the summed cost:**
   - `@consumer` twins: 42% (B9) and 34% (B10).
   - The `review-shard-merge` and `adversarial-shard-merge` families: 33% and 29%. Their 18 units in each push cost 37 to 147 s each.
   - Units rerun only on a legacy directory line (the log's `unattributed` rows, 15 and 13 fixtures): 10% and 7%.
4. **The steps before the suite run concurrently.** Their serial sums are 220 s (B9) and 172 s (B10). At most 120 s and 83 s of wall clock remain for them, and the longest step was backlog receipts, at 97 s and 68 s.

At width 12 the suite remains throughput-bound. Loaded unit costs rise with width, and the hook's own sweep could not separate 12 from 16, so this entry predicts no figure for width 12. The next push run at 12 (the operator's batch-257 ruling) is the measurement. No hand timing run is owed.

Owed:
- (a) `pole_info_step` prints the summed loaded cost ÷ width beside the pole and names whichever bound is larger, from `LASTRUN_OWN` in the same awk. This needs no new fork.
- (b) The two hook headers state the bound the push's own figures show. The `CLAUDE.md` sentence was corrected in this unit, at -1 byte, on the operator's word.
- (c) Time the work `fixture_suite_step` does outside the pool, then cut it.
- (d) Trace the `unattributed` fixtures so that legacy directory lines stop dispatching them.
- (e) Weigh the `@consumer` twin set and the shard-merge lettered units against what each catches (operator ruling "A step with no measured value goes").

Each lettered item expires separately.

Provenance: batch 257, wave 4 (ai-dlc-33), from the B9 and B10 gate logs and the durations record; id allocated by the lead.

**PARTIAL (v0.1136.0) — (a) and (b) shipped; (c), (d) and (e) stay owed.** `pole_info_step` (`.githooks/pre-push`) now prints a second line under the pole: `throughput <sum>s summed over <n> unit(s) / <w> worker(s) = <t>s`, followed by `THROUGHPUT-BOUND` when that figure exceeds the pole and `POLE-BOUND` otherwise. It reads `LASTRUN_OWN` in the same awk, so it adds no fork. The width is `FIXTURE_JOBS`, cut to the number of units timed. A tie names the pole, and a width that is not a count names no bound. `core/fixtures/suite-pole-info` arms 10 to 12 cover these cases, and arms 1 and 9 cover the width cut. The consumer hook has no pole step, so it is unchanged. The step label now names both bounds. For (b), the two `.githooks/pre-push` headers are rewritten. The pole step's header (`3a.`) now names both lower bounds and says that a push dispatching most of the suite is width-bound, with B9's and B10's figures. ## BL-1141 — five s322 step parts read "no measured value", and one sprint cannot decide whether they go

**DEFECT (efficiency).** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-15. Owner: the step text under `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/` that dispatches each part; the fix names the file and line for each one.

BL-812's W9-18 step-value paragraph reads every label that rose on s322 on subagent dollars. Five parts carry no measured value there. Figures are s322, from `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322/out/` at `EXTRACT_WIN_END=2026-11-12T14:41:00Z`.

| Part | s322 cost | s322 reading | Failure case it exists for |
|---|---|---|---|
| carry-over-evaluation p3 (part and cross) | 7 spawns, $13.10, plus a $0.29 deferral record (`co_yield_s322.txt`) | 2 MAJOR, both deferred to requirements and shipped unfixed | a defect the p2 repair wrote into the carry-over evaluation |
| `gate-validation[implementation]` gate QA | 4 seats, $10.45 (`gate_yield_s322.txt`) | 0 C/M and no rework on stories 1, 2, 3 and 5 | a story whose acceptance criteria fail after code review APPROVED |
| `gate-validation[architecture]` adjudicator shards | 10 spawns, $3.81 (`gate_yield_s322.txt`) | 10 checks, 0 FAIL | the architecture step advancing over a failing gate check |
| `gate-validation[retro]` adjudicator shards | 9 spawns, $3.49 (`tail_yield_s322.txt`) | 9 PASS, 0 FAIL | the retro step advancing over a failing gate check |
| requirements PRD validate run | 1 spawn, $1.28 (`req_yield_s322.txt`) | grade Excellent, 0 Critical, 2 Medium, 5 Low; no committed record joins it to a fix | a PRD defect reaching architecture |

"A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`) decides each part, but one sprint never supports removing a pass. A zero-FAIL gate is also judged on consequence, because its catch is rare.

Fix: read the same five parts on s323 once it is complete, with the s322 readers ported to s323's parts and refs.
- A part with a catch on s323 is KEEP.
- A part with no measured value on both sprints is removed or narrowed in its step file, with the projected saving stated.
- For the two adjudicator parts, the reading also weighs consequence. A part judged KEEP on consequence names the failure it guards against.

Dependencies:
- None of the five needs extract.py's classifier, because each is a subagent part partitioned from `spawns.jsonl` by description.
- The s323 extraction does need the s322/s323 sprint edge in extract.py's EDGES, which W9-12 is adding, and the same edge in `lead_class_value.py`'s copy.

P2 counts an UNGUARDED subject with a shebang per SOURCE. ## BL-1161 — no fixture asserts the pre-push `REFUSED.` banner, I66's pool-shadow rule misses several override forms, and a string `)` mis-closes a marked subshell

**NOTE.** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-17. Owner: unassigned (`.githooks/pre-push` and `core/git-hooks/pre-push`, the `FIXTURE_EXIT` span at `.githooks/pre-push:4545-4550` and `core/git-hooks/pre-push:3750-3755`; the pool-shadow rule in the I66 unit of `scripts/validate-enforcement-map.sh`, the awk opened at `:5503`).

This entry carries three distinct claims. It expires only when all three do.

1. No fixture asserts the `pre-push: REFUSED.` banner. `core/fixtures/consumer-suite-pool/run.sh:810-822` asserts exit 2 for a lone refusal on the consumer hook, with an exit-1 twin above it. I66 binds the distribution hook's `FIXTURE_EXIT` tail to be identical to the consumer's (BL-583's batch 258 C5 PARTIAL). No fixture asserts the banner line itself: `grep -c` gives 0 in that fixture, against 2 for `exits 2`. `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/handoff.md` step 3 branches on that line. Owed: extend the exit-2 cell at `:815-816` to assert the `pre-push: REFUSED.` line.
2. I66's pool-shadow rule does not flag these override forms when they are appended outside the pool: `NAME+=`, `for NAME in`, `read -r NAME`, `unset [-f|-v] NAME`, `function NAME {` without parens, `printf -v NAME`, `: ${NAME:=x}` and `: ${NAME=x}`, `eval "NAME=..."` and `alias NAME=`. A ` #` inside a string also truncates the comment strip, and a name the pool only reads is not covered. No live instance was measured. Owed: widen the grammar to these forms, with a probe per form and a re-measured false-positive set.
3. The marker's `( … )` block is scoped by a count of `(` minus `)` that includes parens inside strings. An unbalanced `)` inside a string in a marked subshell (`echo ")"`) closes the block early, so a marked line still inside the subshell is falsely flagged as top-level. This fails loud, not open. The mirror case, an unbalanced `(` that leaves the block open, fails closed: I66 reports an open block at the end of the hook. No live instance was measured. Owed: count only parens outside quotes and comments, with the `echo ")"` probe turning quiet and the `echo "("` probe still failing.

**PARTIAL (v0.1178.0), batch 260 C3.** Claim 2's four unlisted forms are built in the I66 pool-shadow awk. `(( N++ ))`, `(( N = 3 ))`, `$(( --N ))`, `"$(( N++ ))"` and `for (( N=0; ...; N++ ))` print `[arith]` (an assignment operator `=` `+=` `-=` `*=` `/=` `%=` `<<=` `>>=` `&=` `|=` `^=` or `++`/`--` on either side, never `==`; `<=`, `>=`, `!=`, `>` and `==` stay quiet). Arithmetic is read off an image of the line with single-quoted spans and double-quoted spans blanked except a command substitution inside one, so `awk '(( N++ ))'` and `echo "(( N++ ))"` stay quiet. `let N++` and `let "N+=1"` print `[let]` (the `let` word is detected with strings blanked and its arguments read raw, so the string at `.githooks/pre-push:4412` stays quiet). `N[i]=` and `N[i]+=` print without a form. `declare|typeset|local -n X=N` prints `[nameref]`, keyed on the target and read before the `local` strip. The nameref ban was not put in `validate-shell-portability.sh` S3: its corpus is `git ls-files '*.sh'`, which holds neither pre-push hook. False-positive set with the shipping awk: 0 rows over both hooks (the adversary's census outside the pool: 31 `((` lines holding no pool name, 1 `let` line, a string, 0 `N[..]=`, 0 `-n`). Still open: the read-only-names arm of claim 2 (measured, 77-hit set enumerated, not built), a nameref declared without a target and assigned later (`declare -n r` then `r=N`), and the NOTE forms below. Earlier PARTIAL (v0.1167.0): the read-only-names arm of claim 2 and four unlisted forms (now built, above). NOTE: `for N; do`, `select N in`, `getopts ... N`, `trap 'N=...'` and `readonly N` also stay unflagged. The comment strip's quote state is carried across lines (cut() blanks a multi-line string whole), resetting at each hook's start; a hook that ends inside a quote prints `QUOTE` and fails I66, so a desynchronised state fails closed. Found by the tip adversary: with the state reset per line, the line that closes a multi-line `awk '...'` string read as an opening quote, its `)` went uncounted, and a later `a)` case arm rebalanced the marked block, exempting a top-level marked override (base printed MARKTOP; the probe now does again, and the per-line-reset mutant misses it).

1. Built. The exit-2 cell of `consumer-suite-pool` now also asserts the banner line `^pre-push: REFUSED\. A fixture unit made no progress and was killed;` in the hook's output, and the exit-1 twin asserts the line is absent. Cost: one `grep -q` per cell on an existing output file, zero execs of note. Catch on record: with the banner text of `core/git-hooks/pre-push` mutated to `REFUSE.` the fixture reads `FAIL  a lone refusal exited 2 but the hook did not print the pre-push: REFUSED. banner steps/handoff.md step 3 branches on` (`core/fixtures/consumer-suite-pool/run.sh:810-822`, re-run on the final tree), 46 passed and 1 failed, where the cell read only the rc and the unit line before. Who would notice it gone: `steps/handoff.md` step 3 branches on that line, so a reworded banner would send a pipeline agent down the wrong branch. The distribution hook's banner is bound to the consumer's by I66's FIXTURE_EXIT identity, so the consumer hook is the one asserted.

2. Built, with a surviving clause. The pool-shadow awk now reads every listed form over the pool's global and function names (`NAME+=`, `for NAME in`, `read [-r] NAME`, `unset [-f|-v] NAME`, `function NAME`, `printf -v NAME`, `${NAME:=x}` and `${NAME=x}`, `eval ...NAME=...`, `alias NAME=`) and strips the comment quote-aware, so `echo "a # b"; NAME=1` is flagged. Cost: the same single awk invocation, no added fork or exec (the diff adds no command substitution or pipe); the awk body grew by one character-walk per line. Probe per form on an extracted copy of the shipping awk, form appended outside the pool: every one prints `<line> global|function <name> [<form>]`; the same line appended inside the pool and the same form on a non-pool name are quiet; the HEAD awk is quiet on all twelve new probes (the baseline that proves they discriminate). Mutant: disabling the quote tracking in the character walk scores the `echo "a # b"` probe quiet and `echo ")"` loud again. False-positive set: the candidate patterns over both hooks at the tip returned 0 hits, with the HEAD awk's own `X=1` and `X()` probes (hit) as the control in the same run. The clause that SURVIVES is the read-only names: the candidate set (a `$NAME` read in the pool and assigned nowhere at column 0) was 77 hits over the two hooks, all ordinary locals and top-level configuration (`n`, `out`, `rc`, `q`, `sp`, `FXCOUNT_*`, `AI_DLC_*`, `PREPUSH_CL_ENTRY`), so it was not built. Also not covered: `(( NAME++ ))`, `let NAME=`, `NAME[i]=`, `declare -n`.

3. Built. Paren counting for the marked `( ... )` block uses a quote- and comment-blanked copy of the line. The quote state is carried across lines, so a multi-line `awk '` ... `'` string is blanked whole: the line that closes it (`' /dev/null)`) is not read as an opening quote, and a marked top-level override after such a block still prints `MARKTOP`. `( cd /` + `echo ")"` + a marked line + `)` read `MARKTOP` before and is quiet now; so are `echo ')'` and a line whose parens sit only in a string and a trailing comment. The `echo "("` probe's reversal is by design: quote-aware counting balances it, the same rule that quiets `echo ")"`. The fail-closed side is an unbalanced `(` outside quotes: `( cd /` + `foo=(a` + a marked line + `)` still prints `OPEN` at the opener line. Cost: none beyond claim 2's walk. Who would notice it gone: an edit adding a log line with a `)` in a string to a marked subshell, which failed the push loud with a message blaming the wrong line.

**NOTE.** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-18. Owner: `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/_gate-procedures.md:693–698` and the upgrade path that should run `core/scripts/validate-bmad-invocations.sh`.

## BL-1175 — PLANNING, the one entry: planning costs about 40 hours and $900 to $1,300 whatever the sprint is, and every planning-cycle fix is a work item here

**DEFECT (efficiency).** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-18. Owner: `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/route.md` (the intensity classification, lines 527–543), `core/skills/ai-dlc/SKILL.md` Rule 8 (the intensity table, lines 238–253), and the four planning step files (`carry-over-evaluation.md`, `requirements.md`, `architecture.md`, `stories-test-strategy.md`).

**This is the single entry for the cost of the planning cycle, by operator ruling of 2026-11-18.** No other entry is filed for it. A new planning finding becomes a work item below. BL-1169, BL-1170 and BL-1171 are folded in as work items 3, 4 and 2. There is no target number, by operator ruling of 2026-11-18: gains come from removing waste that an honest reading finds, not from a figure chosen in advance. The entry is done when every work item is shipped or closed on its reading AND a complete graph sprint has been measured against the baseline; it is never split, and an item is never moved to another entry.

### What is wrong

`route.md:531` assigns `full` to any sprint with three or more stories touching service code paths, and `SKILL.md:250–253` gives each tier a minimum cycle per planning artifact. One tier is recorded for the whole sprint. Nothing reads what kind of change a story is, so a story that extends existing behaviour or fixes a bug takes the same four document steps and the same review and repair series as a new subsystem, and one story that needs the full cycle puts every story through it.

Measured on graph, read only, in-session time only, the four planning steps with their gates, on the monotone segment clock (`EXTRACT_MONOTONE_SEGS=1`, BL-1174) with the default clock beside it. The intensity is the `validation_intensity` line of graph's `_bmad-output/pipeline-snapshot.md` at each ref.

| Sprint | Graph ref | Intensity | Stories | Planning h, monotone (old clock) | Less operator wait | Token-eq $ (API $) |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| s321 | `ec443477d` | `full` | 25 | 40.8 (43.0) | 36.8 | 1,298 (1,279) |
| s322 | `f7e60625b` | `carry-over-single` | 8 | 36.9 (44.0) | 30.0 | 889 (720) |
| s323 | `16fd227d9` | `full` | 18 | 39.6 (133.1) | 27.0 | 1,071 (876) |

Reading on complete s323 (batch 261; pin EXTRACT_WIN_END=2026-11-20T04:20:00Z; monotone clock unless labelled). s321, s322 and s323 are complete. The `(old clock)` column is the default clock before BL-1174 (`EXTRACT_MONOTONE_SEGS=0`); both columns reproduce at the shipped extractor, and s323's 133.1 h is an artifact of that clock. The s323 row was first taken at `e70a344c0` and pin `2026-11-18T17:54:00Z` with the same figures. Source: `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s323-complete-b261.md` and its `out/` files (`out/s323_complete.txt`).

- The charge does not follow the work. 8, 18 and 25 stories each paid 37 to 41 hours.
- The reduced tier does not reduce it. s322 ran `carry-over-single` and paid 36.9 h and $889.
- Planning is most of a sprint. In s322 it was 36.9 of 66.4 h and $889 of $1,348; implementing all eight stories took 13.0 h and $223.

The planning rounds hold named catches (in s321's stories step, 39 unique survivors in the per-story elicitation shards, including the CRITICAL 17#F-1 on story 4.3, `docs/analysis/step-value-stories-elicitation-s321.md:121`; and 8 in adversarial pass 1, including the CRITICAL 19 F-1 on story 5.2, `docs/analysis/step-value-stories-adversarial-s321.md:194`; corrected in batch 259, C5, from a sentence that gave the elicitation count against the adversarial file), so the work below matches depth to the change and removes no round that holds a catch.

### Work items

Each item states its own acceptance. Items 1 and 2 waited on item 0; items 3 to 6 do not. Item 6 was added in batch 259, C5. What each item shipped or closed on is under "Progress" below.

0. **The reading that sizes items 1 and 2. No code, no new run.** From graph's s321 to s323 planning artifacts and the step-value files: classify each story as carrying a new requirement, a new architecture decision, both or neither; count the surviving requirements-step, architecture-step and stories-step findings raised against each class and against each routing tag. Also read what the requirements and architecture steps' cost scales with (in-scope stories, document parts, shards per pass), because their hours so far do not follow story count: requirements was 11.1, 9.9 and 13.5 h and architecture 10.0, 5.8 and 5.2 h for 25, 8 and 18 stories. That decides what item 1 saves in a mixed sprint. Done when both tables are in this entry.
1. **Tier per story on what the story changes, not per sprint on story count** (`route.md:527–543`, `SKILL.md` Rule 8). A story carrying neither a new requirement nor a new architecture decision does not enter the requirements or architecture review series: those documents name it as out of scope and it enters at the stories step. A sprint made only of such stories runs carry-over evaluation and the stories step. Ships only if item 0 shows such stories hold few or no surviving requirements or architecture findings; otherwise it is closed here with that reading. Ceiling on s323, if no story needed either step: 18.7 h (13.5 + 5.2, of which 6.2 h was operator wait) and $447 ($274 + $173).
2. **Tier the per-story party and elicitation rounds inside the stories step by the routing tag the step already carries** (`stories-test-strategy.md:30`; was BL-1171). Untagged stories take adversarial pass 1 only; capital-path and security-tagged stories keep the full cycle. Ships only if item 0 shows survivors cluster in tagged stories. Estimate: $134 a sprint if 40% of 25 stories are untagged, at s321's $7.49 and $5.96 a story; wall clock moves little because the rounds are parallel.
3. **One readiness run when the first passes, and no file nobody reads** (`architecture.md:262`, `stories-test-strategy.md:18` and `:542`; was BL-1169). Read the three calls' spawns and findings on s321 and s322; a call with no finding that reached a fix goes. The `intent=sprint-planning` output is not produced when nothing consumes its sprint data. Estimate: 0.5 to 1.2 h and $5 to $11 a sprint, on 10 to 20 minutes and $1.50 a call, to be replaced by the measured figures.
4. **The planning-time trace gate that cannot fail moves to sprint review** (`stories-test-strategy.md:677–700`; was BL-1170). At planning, a deterministic check fails on a criterion with no mapped case; the trace runs once at sprint review, where its verdict can read FAIL. Hours and dollars: the planning run's measured cost, read from s321 and s322 before the change. As built in batch 259, C5, the item is a removal only: no AC-to-case check and no sprint-review trace run were added (Progress, item 4).
5. **Pass 2 no wider than what the pass-1 repair changed.** The mechanism is BL-911's and stays there; this item is its planning outcome. On s323 the adversary ran 15 spawns at requirements p1 and 15 at p2, 5 and 5 at architecture, 4, 5 and 4 at carry-over. Join each series' pass-2 width to its changed-part count; if pass 2 is wider than the changed parts plus the cited parts plus one, the defect is reported to BL-911 and fixed there, and this item closes when a sprint shows the narrowed width.
6. **Passes per series** (added batch 259, C5). After pass 1, s321 to s323 ran 28 further adversarial passes. They hold 1 CRITICAL (s321 architecture p4 F-1, introduced by the p3 repair, text written at `architecture-repair-p3.md:373–383`) and 29 first-authored MAJORs (27 of them in s321). Today every MAJOR less the underived ones counts toward NOT_MET (`core/team-roles/adversary.md:441–465`; `validate-adversarial-convergence.sh:706–710`). A MAJOR that a mechanical join places inside the repair made between pass N-1 and pass N stops counting toward NOT_MET; it still gets its targeted fix and a lead check that the convergence validator can see; a CRITICAL always blocks; a finding that cannot be joined blocks. Candidates scored on the record (estimates apportioned by spawns): the partition (b) removes 7 passes, about 4.4 h less operator wait and $97 over the three sprints, losing 0 CRITICAL and 0 first-authored MAJOR, with 20 MAJORs going to targeted fix; a pass cap of 2 removes 15 passes but loses the s321 CRITICAL and 11 first-authored MAJORs, a cap of 3 removes 6 and loses the CRITICAL and 4; candidate (d) is already shipped. The join must read only the previous pass's repair: under an any-earlier-repair join, s321 architecture p3 reads MET and the p4 CRITICAL is lost. Item 6 SHIPS in this release, built in full by operator ruling. Mechanism: the merge snapshots the bytes it reviewed and quotes-joins each CRITICAL/MAJOR against the immediate predecessor pass's snapshot only; a MAJOR is repair-introduced only if ALL its quotes occur exactly once in pass N and 0 times in pass N-1, blocking = major - max(underived, repair_introduced), CRITICAL always blocks, and an unquoted or unjoinable finding blocks. A stem with more than 25% of its lines changed makes every finding blocking, J3 closes repair-introduced keys only as repaired (never deferred), and the gate alone re-derives the count through the merge (arm R). Snapshots are UNTRACKED at `s<N>/adversarial-snapshots/<sha256>` (the directory carries its own `.gitignore`), roughly 270-280 KB per pass per document on disk, never committed. An already-merged pass keeps its recorded count; arm R reports PENDING and does not block, so a lost snapshot degrades to the recorded count and never refuses. A pass merged after its predecessor's snapshot is lost finds every finding unjoinable and blocks. Arm R counts only merge-written passes (those carrying `shard_tool_use_ids:`, as arms B and E do), and a re-merge of an existing pass whose predecessor's snapshot is lost keeps the stored count and answers UNCHANGED. Numbers: measured removal is 0 of 7 passes on today's grammar and 0 of 3 measurable under the ALL rule; the 7 passes, about 4.4 h and $97 over s321-s323 is a CEILING (estimate), and the real joinable share is first measurable on graph's first sprint after the pull, because the quote grammar arrives with the reconcile PR. Calibration of the 25% ceiling (changed share between consecutive passes): s321 architecture p3 to p4 18.2%, s321 test-strategy p4 to p5 10.6%, s323 coe p1 to p2 16.5%, s322 spine p1 to p2 49.7%; the last is over the ceiling, so all its findings stay blocking.
